QF.id: Securities Types Features and Asset Allocation Concepts_36

question.text: Share warrants issued by a company give the holder:

answer.text: The right but not the obligation to subscribe to a specific number of equity shares at a predetermined price on or after a predetermined date
The obligation to purchase equity shares at market price on the exercise date
Immediate ownership of equity shares without any additional payment
The right to receive dividends without owning any equity shares

explanation.text: The Logic: Share warrants give the holder the right, but not the obligation, to subscribe to a specific number of equity shares at a predetermined price on or after a predetermined date. Investors pay 25% upfront; on exercise they pay the balance and shares are allotted. If not exercised, the upfront amount is forfeited. The Trap: Warrants give rights, not obligations (option B). They do not confer immediate share ownership (option C) — shares are allotted only upon exercise. There is no dividend right without share ownership (option D). Note: The 25% upfront payment, allotment on exercise, balance payment, and forfeiture on non-exercise are the source-listed mechanics for warrants.
